newsitem.title: POLAND: Zasada launches Mercedes vans production.
newsitem.headline: Zasada launches Mercedes vans production.

text.p: Poland's automotive group Sobieslaw Zasada Centrum SA on Tuesday launched the construction of Mercedes' mini-vans Vito, under a first production licence granted by the German car maker in the eastern Europe.

Zasada said in a statement on Tuesday that its plant Vito-Jelcz sp. z o.o., based in south-eatern Poland, would manufacture 400 mini-vans this year, more than 3,000 next year and at least 10,000 in 1998.
"Mercedes' licence is the company's first granted for car production in an east European country," the statement said.
It said the company would seek to win a 25 percent share of Poland's mini-van market, which is forecast to grow to 42,000 units sold this year from nearly 33,000 in 1995.
Zasada, which controls two utility car factories and several automotive parts plants, is Mercedes' sole distributor in Poland.
Vito-Jelcz is a fully-owned subsidiary of ZS Jelcz SA truck maker, 84-percent owned by the Zasada group.
